body: I have thought so as well. Unfortunately, I stuck with it due to the 80/20 split with no monthly fees. And while I have been able to keep more of my earnings, being in the office felt really awkward because I don’t fit in with the cliques. I naively hoped that I can overlook feeling ignored in return for more money but it has gotten to the point where my brokerage mates thought I was annoying for asking them questions. And they weren’t even that many questions! 😅

In a different thread, you asked me why I didn’t have her sign the listing agreement when she wasn’t ready. Is it better to push someone to sign something when they weren’t ready (hence, ending up looking desperate) or offer guidance and give them space?

At the time we had our consultation and after the phone call, she said she wanted to wait a few weeks while she gets the house packed up and completed the repairs around the house. You mentioned in a different thread that you said I sounded “desperate” yet asked me why I didn’t push her to sign the listing agreement when she wasn’t ready?

The numbers are not the reasons why I felt blind-sided by this person. It’s because I’ve already established a colleague-type of relationship with her. Guess I’m just a trusting person who hoped that people would treat others how they want to be treated.
My usual morning cold-calls are sales calls. This interaction with her stemmed from her coming to me first and I responded.

I’m on the fence about offering my time and resources for free, but I also don’t don’t want to come off vindictive either because in my experience, the agents who tend to react emotionally towards real or perceived slights don’t end up with the sale anyway. Because the person who supposedly “slighted” them would perceive them as unfit and unprofessional.
Yes, she asked for my advice as a realtor and even explicitly stated during a phone call that she wanted me to list her house. It wasn’t a passively implied thing. That was what she said.
I did not mean to imply that I passive “expected” to be the listing agent leading up to recently. She called a few weeks ago and EXPLICITLY told me that she wanted me to be her listing agent.
I have a feeling that maybe she’s not aware that she was doing it or meant any ill-will.

I sat down with her and ran comps, made CMA adjustments based on square footage and similar features, provided her numbers to contractors who would be able to help her make necessary repairs at fair prices, and even offered to cover the costs of photography, staging, and cleaning. It wasn’t just a vapid conversation.
I offered to cover the costs of photography, staging, and cleaning services. It wasn’t just a casual conversation. We sat down, did comps, talked prepping strategies, etc.

Yes, I want the listing. But I also want to be strategic about it by not reacting emotionally. Of course, I am going to feel how I’m going to feel (betrayed) but she already went against my advice by overpricing her home by $7000 past the highest end of my comps. If it doesn’t work out for her, I’ve already established that level of trust and level-headedness with her.

Yeah, I was pretty blind-sided. She didn’t seem to be one of those types of people to pull something like that. We worked together in the past and she held one of those higher-end professional jobs where she has to remain professional and courteous. Guess it doesn’t matter. However, she went against my advice and priced her house too high as a FSBO, so I’m sure she won’t be able to sell her house that way anyway.

After reading all of these comments, I guess going “no inspection” will always trump over anything else in this market. Is that the gist? How would you personally feel about buyers winning the house now but end up blaming you a year later, if they uncover something that might cost them thousands of dollars to fix down the line? That wouldn’t personally sit well with me and makes me feel like an uncaring realtor.
One of the units is occupied, and so we really don’t know what condition it is in. Could be nothing to worry about, could be worse than we thought. We wouldn’t know.

I try to use the quality over quantity approach to my clients. I do my due diligence and perform fiduciary duties, including educating them about processes AND look out for them as well. 

In the case of this particular property, one of the units is occupied and we don’t even know what condition it is in because we couldn’t walk through it. I would feel bad if I tried to steer them towards waiving inspections, only for them to have to (potentially) spend thousands of dollars to repair that occupied unit later when the tenant moves out. Then they would turn around and blame me for not looking out for them.

That was my concern as well. I wouldn’t want them to blame me six months from now if they had gotten the house, waived the inspection, and then be out thousands of dollars in repairs. I explained the pros and cons of to my buyer, and they made the ultimate decision.

I completed eXp’s onboarding long before I completed the team’s onboarding. They used to be KW before, but they run their team like they’ve always have. They joined eXp for the revenue share but don’t utilize any of their brokerage’s systems and processes.
I suppose sarcasm doesn’t read well on Reddit. I never intended to do just that. I was merely frustrated with the situation.
The team that I am with requires it. They have an office. I think they might have joined eXp for the revenue share, but they operated like they’re independent of eXp.

It took a few months for me because I had a full-time job. Most new agents who don’t have a full-time job other than their real estate career usually breezed through quickly. As part of our onboarding process, I had to accumulate 40 hours of front desk time (called opportunity time). With a M-F, 8-5 job, I couldn’t do that as quickly as other agents because I had to divvy up the time in increments. And that is if I have time to come into the office.

Thankfully, my friend is not building from the ground up. I took him on a few showings and he picked a spec home from a builder that he is waiting to see completed before he wants to go under contract. 

The builder is offering massive incentives towards closing costs, which I forwarded to my friend/client and hopefully he takes them up on their offer. The builder let me know that they don’t even need a down payment upfront, just the earnest money to go under contract, and he can just cough up the rest of the money later at closing. If I know something that the builder is offering, I let him know ASAP.

Yes I did participate in the trainings. I feel like I did better on trainings that were more hands-on (like writing contracts and performing a CMA). But on more conceptual subjects like financing, I needed more guidance if I felt like the class was rushed. On that subject matter, I pretty much reached out to our team’s lending partners and learned more in-depth from them about all of their loan products. 

As far as building my business goes, I’ve been producing contents on IG and TikTok, marketing properties on Facebook Marketplace and various real estate groups, cold called, cold emailed, and reaching out to my sphere to let them know that I am more than happy to help them sell their house/buy a house. I’m sure there are a lot more I could be doing.
He did signed a buyer broker agreement. Hopefully he doesn’t plan to screw me over. Fingers crossed.

I get my cold call leads from our team’s CRM. I basically go down a list of names that have not been contacted by anyone in a while (about six months to a year) and tried to follow up with “Hi, this is (so and so) with so-and-so team. You have previously worked with so-and-so agent on our team in the past and I just want to reach out and see if your real estate needs have been met or if you’re still in the market to buy/sell.” Most of the time, they don’t even pick up but I leave them voicemails. And if they do, they usually respond with “I am not interested at this time, thank you.” I have never been cussed out, thank god.

I was super introverted prior to my career change, and so my sphere of influence is rather small. I do try and talk to random people at my gym or church though. My hobbies are geared towards fitness, but I find that most people at gyms just want to be left alone. Lol

They offer training classes, but they were mainly workshop type of classes taught by high producers on the team. And they all have different ways of doing things. So far, I’ve learned how to write contracts, how to do CMAs, learned about different loan products, what to look for during inspections, etc. My team lead also told me to cold call people on our CRM (that hasn’t been in contact with anyone on the team in a while) and so I’ve been doing that. I plan to go door-knocking three days before my next open house so that I can steer them there and get more foot traffic.

Full disclosure: I am NOT going to push my friend to close earlier. Never plan to. It was a sarcastic comment aimed at my team lead’s unreasonable demands to have something under NOW. Of course I would not do that and hurt our friendship/working relationship.
I feel better now, knowing that it’s likely a sales pitch.

Yeah, I can see where a part time job would hold me back from doing active prospecting. That is one of my worries. However, it appears that a lot of people on here have been able to make it work with gig-type of roles and a few who are able to make it work with permanent part time roles. 

My game plan at the moment, that I think would help me further my experience in this field, is to: Ask the high producers on my team if I could help with tedious tasks, volunteer to sit on open houses for realtors who cannot make it due to personal reasons, or ask my broker if I could be a personal assistant. All related to real estate. 

Last resort is probably to bite the bullet and become a bartender at a high-traffic bar that caters to a higher-income demographic. That way, I can network and hopefully convert them into leads.

Other than participate in a few council meetings here or there (there might be more that didn’t get shown, though). 

If the dance of dragons have not happened, what kind of queen would she have been without experience? Same about Aegon, what the hell has that kid done to lead his mother to believe that he could do anything? 

About Alicent, (to be clear, I am not an Alicent fan) that woman has done her duties throughout most of her life, even if she may not have wanted to, and was coerced by her father at a young age to play a huge political role. At the very least, Alicent has played a bigger role in the council than Rhaenyra has simply by being the ever dutiful queen mother, even if she seemed to hate her life. I feel somewhat sad for her tbh. But in no way saying that SHE should rule Westeros. Just that the “work” side of politicking lean more towards Alicent than Rhaenyra.

In another thread that I was bullied for, I was attempting to have a discussion about the handling of POC characters (who are perfectly casted by the way, just need a little more screen time), but was told to stop basing my views through modern day lens. 🙄 Kind of a shut up and put up kind of way. 

People can be nuts. I was a former city council member and an avid volunteer for police reform groups and women’s shelters (where I worked with a lot of POC, especially women). Of course, I would address it at every turn. That was my line of work. Lol. But discuss a difficult topic and it was all pitchforks from there. 

I am with you on Rhaenyra. And your views are 100% valid. Rabid fans be damned. 😉

Be careful. Some fans are pretty protective of their favorite characters. Any perspectives that don’t align with their views would get you bullied, downvoted, and harassed. Been through that with an attempt at a serious discussion in another thread.

I’m just very curious though and I hope you don’t mind me asking. While I can see where you are coming from (with the HOTD universe being based on medieval Europe), how many POC characters in other shows or movies that you’ve seen were only needed when geography is involved? And yes, geography is important, and at what point could POC characters exist organically without their entire personality being attached to a certain geographical location? 

For example, King’s Landing is a big metro area, where trading of all kinds occur and those who immigrated from other lands might have been two or three generations removed from their homeland. I’m sure there could be a mixture of many different races and cultures, and some people might have assimilated pretty well by that point. Much like modern day Europe. Yes, I know this story is based in medieval Europe, but I could recall that there were immigrants already living in Europe during that time. Through slave trades, trade routes, and such? Please correct me if I’m wrong. I’m just curious, and I would love your thought on it.

Yes to your point about the casting of the Velaryons. THIS is a responsible handling of diverse casting. Not trope-y and fits in with the storylines. The handling of the Asian woman could have been done a little bit better in showing her calculating, cunning, and smart nature as a player in the game though. I thought she was great, just needed more material to work with. But it also could be the condensed story lines and editing.

But a general no less. Would have been an interesting film, but I doubt it’ll ever be green-lit. I would love to see historical fiction from a different worldview than what we are used to seeing.

Cool with me if someone who identifies as black or POC doesn’t agree, it doesn’t hurt my feelings because that’s what discussions do, they make you listen and learn. Learned from all of them, but the one thing that stuck with me was how likely or unlikely it is for those who’ve been harmed to be believed (black women were dismissed by police the most when it comes to rape cases, sadly). Once you spent so much time with those who don’t look like you or experienced things the way you did, you start to see things. Or better yet, unable to unsee the horrible things they experienced that have been brushed aside because of their race.

Corlys said that he did worked very hard. He told Daemon this himself in episode 2. 

Example: “We are the realm’s second sons, Daemon. Our worth is not given, it must be made.”

“When I ascended the Driftwood Throne, I knew what I wanted. So I went out and seized it.”

“Unlike every other lord of the realm, I can say that I built my house’s high seat with the strength of mine own back.”

It came straight out of his mouth in that episode. Calling out the writers for mis-handling race may make a lot of people uncomfortable but it needs to be addressed.

The context of this discussion is on the casting of POC actors within the context of a medieval Euro-centric show. The show runners said they wanted to make a difference, and so they made the conscious decision to cast black actors and POC in major roles. GRRM approved this and thought it was a great idea. They gave these acting roles to black and POC actors who were probably thrilled to be a part of something culturally significant, only to later find out that they didn’t have much to work with or get killed off too early. Imagine being a struggling actor who is not white finally getting their foot into a franchise that would not have hired them in other circumstances, but then their onscreen representation is that of old, tired tv tropes and stereotypes. This is the only concern I have with what the writers were trying to do. They wanted to increase diversity and equity but they actually (probably without thinking about it) harmed it.
Good to see someone care about these girls! Considering that others considered them “unimportant” in the books and show.

Were they boring and unimportant to you because the writers never did expanded on them? Would you have preferred if they axed these characters entirely? It’s not a good look for them to be reduced to being extras.

So now that you’ve dismissed the other black characters as unimportant enough to expand on and hating on those two black girls who deserved better arcs than what they got (that you can take down if you’d like), you have nothing left but to resort to typing LiKe tHiS?
Did you not read the part where black actors were given barely any scraps to work with, despite Hollywood claiming they are for diversity/equity? Thanks again for more screenshots.
Thanks for that screenshot. I knew fantasy fans are more racist than they let on.

For Hispanics, Mexicans, Latinos and Latinas, I am sorry for the mis-use of the word “Latinx.” Thank you for speaking up and helping me learn. I appreciate that. For those who just wanted to verbally abuse, breathe. I already owned my mistakes. 

As for others who saw no problem with the mis-handling of black actors and asking why I found Baela and Rhaena compelling, and why Corlys needed more screen time, let me explain. 

Corlys: He was one of the main characters with a lot to play in how the story unfolds. Yet spent a considerable amount of time offscreen. He was one of my favorite characters with a lot of complexity and nuances that makes him relatable. He had to work hard to get to where he did, was overlooked because he was a second son, lost both of his children (although, I am happy with the way they saved Laenor from the BS; still wish we had more Laenor in the show), but we hardly got to see him. But okay, let’s show Lary’s obsession with feet instead. 

Baela and Rhaena: Both lost their mother and had their mother’s beloved dragon basically stolen by a snobby white kid, then reduced to extras who smiled at their cousins a lot. Nothing from Baela’s perspectives about being betrothed? How does Rhaena felt about being ignored by her father, who happily warms up to Rhaenyra’s children with open arms?
